newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Dhaka Stock Exchange relaxes rules.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Dhaka Stock Exchange relaxes rules.

text.p: Bangladesh's Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) on Monday relaxed the rule of limiting price movement for any company offering "price-sensitive information".
A statement issued by the DSE late on Sunday said the measure had been taken under an order from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the country's market watchdog.

It said if any listed company supplied price-sensitive information to the DSE the bid limits (plus/minus 10 percent) would not be applicable to any securities of that company for the succeeding three market days.
The bid limit, which restricts price movements of shares within a 10 percent range from their previous rate, was set on October 12.
The step was taken in the wake of a sharp rise in the share prices mainly because of rumours and heavy demand from hundreds of retail investors.
Price-sensitive information the DSE said might influence the market included profit and loss account, dividends, and deals with foreign firms on trade collaboration or technical assistance.
